details.description: Multiple API keys and secrets are hardcoded in source code, exposing sensitive credentials.
details.fix_explanation: Moved secrets to environment variables and fail if missing to avoid storing credentials in source control.

details.description: MD5 is used to derive authentication tokens which is cryptographically weak.
details.fix_explanation: Replaced MD5 with HMAC-SHA256 using server-side secret to generate tokens securely.

details.description: User-controlled input is formatted directly into an SQL query using string interpolation.
details.fix_explanation: Use parameterized SQL queries and validate uid as integer to prevent injection.
details.secure_code_snippet: c.execute("SELECT id, name, balance FROM profiles WHERE id = ?", (int(uid),))

details.description: Usage of subprocess.Popen with shell=True and user-supplied command may allow command injection.
details.fix_explanation: Use Python's zipfile module and sanitize archive name to avoid invoking the shell.

details.description: notify_url from user input is sent to requests.post without validation allowing SSRF to internal services.
details.fix_explanation: Validate scheme (https) and restrict hostnames via ALLOWED_NOTIFY_HOSTS env var; use request timeouts.
details.secure_code_snippet: parsed = urlparse(url); if parsed.scheme != 'https': raise ValueError('notify_url must use https')

details.description: update_records opens an arbitrary file path provided by user which may allow reading sensitive files.
details.fix_explanation: Restrict file access to a specific 'configs' directory and normalize path to prevent traversal.

details.description: Running Flask with debug=True in production can leak sensitive information and enable code execution.
details.fix_explanation: Change debug mode to be controlled by an environment variable and default to False.
